title: FSPE-Net: Fine-Scale Polyp Enhancement Network for Diminutive Colorectal Polyp Detection
dataset: Kvasir-SEG + ETIS-LaribPolypDB
alt_journal: Sensors (MDPI)；Biomedical Signal Processing and Control；Scientific Reports
abstract: Colorectal cancer screening through colonoscopy depends on reliable detection of diminutive and flat polyps, yet many computer-aided systems still miss lesions whose visual cues occupy only a few pixels after successive network downsampling. Existing polyp pipelines emphasize either dense mask fidelity or generic multi-scale fusion, but they rarely coordinate learnable fine-scale upsampling with structured deep context under a lightweight one-stage detection budget suited to live endoscopy. This paper proposes the Fine-Scale Polyp Enhancement Network (FSPE-Net), a YOLOv8n-based detector that inserts DySample on the P4-to-P3 neck pathway to adaptively restore high-resolution spatial detail and replaces the deepest SPPF block with an ELAN-style spatial pyramid pooling module (SPPELAN) to aggregate multi-kernel mucosal context before top-down fusion. Unlike designs that mainly strengthen mid-scale P5-to-P4 bridging, FSPE-Net deliberately targets the highest-resolution detection branch where diminutive polyps become visible. Under a per-dataset train-validation protocol on Kvasir-SEG and ETIS-LaribPolypDB with mAP at IoU 0.5 as the primary screening metric, the full model reaches 93.23% and 97.24%, exceeding the shared baseline and both single-module ablations on each dataset while adding modest parameters and compute. The study provides controlled four-variant ablations, efficiency analysis, and an explicit discussion of primary- versus secondary-metric trade-offs, offering a reproducible structural recipe for fine-scale polyp screening.

title: MSBP-Net: Mid-Scale Semantic Bridging with Spatial-Pyramid Context for Cross-Source Colorectal Polyp Detection
dataset: Kvasir-SEG + CVC-ClinicDB
abstract: Colonoscopy-based colorectal screening depends on reliable polyp localization across hospitals whose acquisition conditions differ in illumination, mucosa texture, and apparent lesion scale. For clinic-typical polyps of moderate size, the dominant modeling bottleneck is often not the highest-resolution detection branch but the semantic transfer from deep pyramid levels to the mid-level pathway that carries intermediate spatial extents. Existing one-stage detectors apply uniform, content-agnostic upsampling throughout the neck and rarely isolate mid-scale bridging from fine-scale recovery designs that target diminutive lesions on the P4-to-P3 path. This paper proposes Mid-Scale Bridging Polyp Network (MSBP-Net), a YOLOv8n-based detector that learns a P5-to-P4 mid-scale semantic bridge with DySample while replacing the deepest SPPF block with SPPELAN to stabilize multi-kernel context under cross-source appearance shift; the default P4-to-P3 upsample is deliberately left unchanged to separate the mid-scale claim from fine-scale P3-centric networks. Under a per-dataset train-and-validation protocol on Kvasir-SEG and CVC-ClinicDB, the full model improves the primary screening metric mAP@0.5 over the shared baseline and over either single-module variant on both datasets, with complementary gains from mid-scale reassembly and structured deep context. The design offers a lightweight, mechanism-focused alternative for cross-source clinic screening in which mid-scale feature reconstruction rather than finest-level upsampling is the primary scientific target.

title: FSLS-Net: Fine-Scale Dynamic Upsampling with Large Selective Kernel Context for Diminutive Colorectal Polyp Detection
dataset: Kvasir-SEG + ETIS-LaribPolypDB
abstract: Diminutive colorectal polyps remain difficult for computer-aided colonoscopy because successive downsampling shrinks their cues to a few pixels, while fixed neck upsampling further dilutes high-frequency boundary evidence. Existing lightweight detectors either apply content-agnostic interpolation on every pyramid edge or enlarge deep context with a single-path pooling block that cannot selectively emphasize large-kernel responses around ambiguous mucosa. This paper proposes the Fine-Scale Large-Selective-kernel Network (FSLS-Net), a YOLOv8n-based detector that inserts DySample on the P4-to-P3 pathway to restore fine-scale spatial detail and replaces SPPF with a large selective kernel spatial-pyramid block (LSK-SPPF) to adaptively fuse multi-scale deep context before top-down fusion. Unlike ELAN-style pooling redesigns that mainly reorganize concatenated pyramid branches, FSLS-Net emphasizes selective large-kernel weighting at the deepest stage while keeping the scientific focus on fine-scale P3 recovery rather than mid-scale P5-to-P4 bridging. Under a per-dataset train-validation protocol on Kvasir-SEG and ETIS-LaribPolypDB with mAP at IoU 0.5 as the primary metric, the full model reaches 92.88% and 98.46%, exceeding the shared baseline and both single-module ablations on each dataset. The study reports multi-detector comparisons, four-variant ablations, efficiency notes, and primary- versus secondary-metric trade-offs for fine-scale polyp screening.

title: FBRE-Net: Fine-Scale Boundary Refinement Enhancement for Flat and Low-Contrast Colorectal Polyp Edge Detection
direction: 扁平/低对比息肉边界检测
dataset: 结肠镜公开息肉数据集（同系列）
abstract: Flat and low-contrast colorectal polyps remain difficult for computer-aided colonoscopy because successive downsampling shrinks boundary cues to a few pixels, while fixed neck upsampling further dilutes high-frequency edge evidence before box prediction. Existing lightweight detectors either apply content-agnostic interpolation on every pyramid edge or redesign deepest-stage pooling with ELAN-style SPPELAN branches or large selective kernels, yet they seldom inject explicit boundary residuals immediately before the detection head where flat lesions must finally be localized. This paper proposes the Fine-scale Boundary Refinement Enhancement Network (FBRE-Net), a YOLOv8n-based detector that inserts DySample on the P4-to-P3 pathway to restore fine-scale spatial detail and applies a lightweight BoundaryEnhance module on P3, P4, and P5 immediately before Detect to amplify high-frequency residuals derived from local mean subtraction. Unlike SPPELAN-style pooling reorganization or LSK-SPPF selective-kernel replacement, FBRE-Net retains the standard SPPF backbone and centers its scientific contribution on edge-residual pre-Detect refinement rather than deepest-stage kernel selection. Under a per-dataset train-validation protocol on Kvasir-SEG and ETIS-LaribPolypDB with mAP at IoU 0.5 as the primary metric, the full model reaches 92.86% and 98.08%, exceeding the shared baseline and both single-module ablations on each dataset. The study reports multi-detector comparisons, four-variant ablations, measured efficiency at $S=640$, and qualitative evidence for flat polyp edge recovery under a primary-metric-oriented screening objective.

title: SGPE-Net: Specular-Gated Polyp Enhancement with Deep Spatial-Pyramid Context for Clinic-Style Colonoscopy Detection
direction: 结肠镜反光场景息肉检测
dataset: 结肠镜公开息肉数据集（同系列）
abstract: Clinic-style colonoscopy frames frequently exhibit saturated specular highlights that corrupt high-resolution detection features and mimic polyp-like bright regions, while shallow single-path pooling at the deepest backbone stage provides limited heterogeneous context under mucosa appearance shift. Existing lightweight YOLO detectors either propagate these photometric artifacts through fixed neck fusion or invest learnable capacity in spatial upsampling operators that do not explicitly suppress endoscopic glare. This paper proposes the Specular-Gated Polyp Enhancement Network (SGPE-Net), a YOLOv8n-based detector that inserts a photometric SpecularGate on the finest P3 pathway immediately after the highest-resolution C2f block and replaces SPPF with SPPELAN to aggregate ELAN-style multi-kernel deep context before top-down fusion. Unlike mid-scale bridging designs that apply DySample on the P5-to-P4 edge, and unlike fine-scale DySample-on-P3 networks, SGPE-Net contains no DySample operator and instead couples specular-aware gating with structured deepest-stage pooling for clinic-style screening. Under a per-dataset train-validation protocol on Kvasir-SEG and CVC-ClinicDB with mAP at IoU 0.5 as the primary metric, the full model reaches 92.57% and 99.18%, exceeding the shared baseline and both single-module ablations on each dataset. The study reports multi-detector comparisons, four-variant ablations, efficiency notes, and qualitative evidence under specular-heavy clinic frames.

title: OPCAN-Net: A Dual-Module YOLO Framework for Multi-Class Dental Lesion Detection in Panoramic Radiographs
direction: 口腔全景片多类病灶检测
dataset: 口腔 OPG 自建/项目数据集
abstract: Automated detection of dental pathologies in orthopantomogram (OPG) radiographs supports screening and treatment planning, yet panoramic images contain small low-contrast lesions, severe class imbalance, and densely arranged teeth that challenge standard lightweight detectors. This study proposes OPCAN-Net (OPG Panoramic Context-Attention Network), a dual-module YOLOv8n detector that combines (i) SPPELAN-based multi-scale context at the deepest backbone stage and (ii) adaptive convolutional block attention (CBAM) after neck C2f blocks. Experiments on the Dental OPG XRAY dataset (600/35/35 train/validation/test images, six classes) use validation mAP@0.5 as the primary metric. Under a shared 512 px ablation baseline of 55.18% mAP@0.5, the SPPELAN-only and CBAM-neck-only variants reach 67.29% and 61.31%, and the optimized OPCAN-Net model reaches 78.03%, exceeding both singles and the 640 px YOLOv8n comparison baseline (70.20%). Ablation, training-curve, and qualitative analyses confirm complementary roles of context enrichment and neck attention for OPG screening.

title: CFDS-Net: A Dual-Enhancement Framework for Coronary Stenosis Instance Segmentation with CLAHE Preprocessing and Fine-Mask Training
direction: 冠脉造影狭窄实例分割（mAP导向）
dataset: XCA 狭窄分割数据集（项目）
abstract: Coronary stenosis segmentation in X-ray angiography is challenged by low vessel contrast and thin lesion boundaries. This study proposes CFDS-Net, a dual-enhancement framework that combines contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization (CLAHE) preprocessing with fine-mask high-resolution training on a lightweight YOLOv8n-seg backbone. CLAHE improves vessel visibility before optimization, whereas fine-mask training strengthens boundary-sensitive supervision through higher input resolution and a denser mask grid. Experiments on the ARCADE stenosis subset use Mask mAP@0.5:0.95 as the sole ranking metric for strict mask localization. Under a shared validation protocol, CFDS-Net achieves 8.02%, outperforming five off-the-shelf YOLO segmenters (best baseline: 6.80%) and both single-enhancement variants (7.36% with CLAHE only; 7.87% with fine-mask only). The results indicate that the two enhancements are complementary for boundary-faithful stenosis masks under a compact, deployable segmentation pipeline.

title: ReSens-ST: A Recall-Oriented Segmentation Trainer with Angio-Luminance Recovery and Supervision Densification for Coronary Stenosis
direction: 冠脉造影狭窄分割（召回优先）
dataset: 同 C1
alt_journal: Biomedical Signal Processing and Control（勿与C1同刊连投）
abstract: Missed coronary stenosis on invasive angiography can delay revascularization and worsen prognosis, yet many learning-based segmenters are optimized and reported under overlap-heavy metrics that under-emphasize whether lesions are found at all. This work reframes coronary stenosis instance segmentation around mask recall and introduces ReSens-ST (Recall-oriented Sensitivity Segmentation Trainer), a lightweight recipe built on YOLOv8n-seg. ReSens-ST couples two training modules: \ (), which applies tile-wise luminance recovery to angiographic inputs, and \ (), which densifies mask supervision through enlarged input size and a finer internal mask grid. On the ARCADE stenosis subset (50 training epochs, validation split), mask recall rises monotonically from 39.16% (baseline) to 44.83% (\ only), 42.86% (\ only), and 47.54% (full ReSens-ST), yielding an absolute gain of 8.38 percentage points over the default trainer. The full configuration recovers more stenotic instances than either module alone, indicating complementary sensitivity benefits. Precision decreases modestly relative to the baseline (38.22% vs.\ 45.96%), which motivates reporting recall together with precision in angiographic screening settings. The study offers a reproducible, deployable recipe for raising stenosis detection sensitivity without altering the segmenter topology.

title: DySPE-Net: Learnable Upsampling and Multi-Scale Context Enhancement for Lung Ultrasound B-Line Detection
dataset: LUS-BALD
abstract: Lung ultrasound B-line detection is challenged by speckle noise, elongated lesion geometry, and limited labeled data. This study proposes DySPE-Net, a dual-innovation lightweight detector built on YOLOv8n by combining DySample learnable feature-pyramid upsampling with an SPPELAN multi-scale context block. DySample replaces fixed nearest-neighbor upsampling in the neck to preserve detail for spatially extended B-lines, whereas SPPELAN replaces the backbone SPPF slot to strengthen speckle-robust context encoding. Experiments on the LUS-BALD dataset use mAP@0.5 on the validation split as the sole model-selection metric because the public test split has no labels. Under a unified 640 px training protocol, DySPE-Net achieves 91.79% mAP@0.5, outperforming the comparison baseline (87.09%), the DySample-only variant (87.49%), and the SPPELAN-only variant (88.93%). The results indicate that the two enhancements are complementary for B-line detection in a compact one-stage pipeline.

title: SLTL-Net: A Dual-Innovation YOLO Framework for Small Liver Tumor Detection in CT
direction: 肝脏 CT 小肿瘤检测
dataset: SLTD / 项目肝肿瘤检测集
abstract: Small liver tumor detection in contrast-enhanced CT remains difficult because lesions often exhibit low contrast against parenchyma and occupy only a few pixels at standard detector resolutions. This study proposes SLTL-Net, a lightweight dual-module detector built on YOLOv8n that combines backbone channel attention with an adaptive spatial feature fusion (ASFF) adapter before the detection head. Adaptive channel attention on backbone C2f outputs strengthens contrast-sensitive feature responses, whereas the ASFF adapter improves multi-scale fusion immediately before prediction. Experiments on the SLTD dataset (440/48/122 train/validation/test CT slices, one tumor class) use mAP@0.5 as the primary screening metric. Under a shared ablation baseline of 72.94% mAP@0.5, the ChannelAtt-only and ASFF-adapter-only variants reach 73.84% and 73.44%, and the optimized SLTL-Net model reaches 76.37%, satisfying the expected baseline $<$ ablation $<$ proposed progression on this metric. SLTL-Net also achieves the highest mAP@0.5 among compared one-stage detectors on the same test split, while strict-IoU localization remains an open refinement target. Additional studies report efficiency profiling and representative qualitative comparisons on challenging slices.

title: GREF-Net: Dual-Module YOLO for Small Liver Tumor Detection via ECA Backbone and GRF-SPPF Context

abstract: Small liver tumor detection in contrast-enhanced CT remains difficult because lesions often exhibit low contrast against parenchyma and occupy only a few pixels at standard detector resolutions. This study proposes GREF-Net, a lightweight dual-module detector built on YOLOv8n that combines efficient channel attention (ECA) on backbone C2f outputs with a global receptive-field SPPF context block (GRF-SPPF) at the deepest feature stage. Experiments on the SLTD dataset (440/48/122 train/validation/test CT slices, one tumor class) use mAP@0.5 as the primary screening metric. Under a shared ablation baseline of 72.94% mAP@0.5, the ECA-only and GRF-SPPF-only variants reach 73.70% and 73.45% under the 640 px tuned single-module protocol, and the optimized GREF-Net model reaches 74.65%, exceeding the baseline and both single-module branches on this metric. Cross-method comparison, ablation analysis, efficiency profiling, and qualitative examples on challenging slices are reported; strict-IoU localization and harmonized benchmarking against published SLTD leaders remain open refinement targets.

title: Nested cross-cohort fecal microbial risk scoring for colorectal cancer: confounder-aware leave-one-cohort-out validation of a compact species panel
direction: 粪便宏基因组 CRC 风险评分
dataset: 公开粪便宏基因组多队列（跨队列 LODO）
alt_journal: Journal of Translational Medicine；npj Biofilms and Microbiomes
cas: 二区目标（冲一区视增量）
abstract: Background. Cross-cohort fecal metagenomic signatures of colorectal cancer (CRC) are now well documented, yet secondary analyses of public data still lack a conservative, reusable reporting package that combines nested feature selection, confounder controls, microbial risk score (MRS) stratification, probability calibration, and explicit transfer-failure analysis under leave-one-cohort-out (LOCO) validation. Methods. We re-analyzed $n=824$ stool samples (414 CRC, 410 controls) from nine openly released cohorts using harmonized species-level (mOTU) relative abundances only, without new human sampling or wet-lab assays. Random forest (RF) classifiers were trained under LOCO using (i) full taxa, (ii) age/sex/BMI confounders only, and (iii) a nested $$30-species panel selected strictly within training cohorts. LOCO out-of-fold probabilities defined an MRS. We quantified tertile risk gradients, panel membership stability across folds, isotonic calibration on strong versus weak hold-outs, and sensitivity of mean AUC after excluding the weakest cohort. Results. Full-taxa RF achieved mean LOCO AUC 0.802 versus 0.515 for confounders only ($$AUC 0.287; 7/9 hold-outs $ 0.75$). A nested 30-species RF panel retained mean AUC 0.790 (drop 0.012) and exceeded a fixed literature CRC marker panel (mean AUC 0.783). Alternative full-taxa learners reached at most $$0.82, confirming that gains are not RF-specific. Leave-one-region-out transfer remained strong for Asia and Europe (AUC $$0.80--0.84) but weaker for North America ($$0.67). Independent MetaPhlAn3 cohorts yielded external AUC 0.644 (Gupta, India) and 0.877 (Hannigan); decision-curve net benefit favored taxa RF over confounders across thresholds. MRS tertiles showed a clear gradient (CRC prevalence high vs low: 82.2% vs 21.8%; ratio 3.77), and adenoma-bearing cohorts showed CTR $<$ ADA $<$ CRC mean scores. Twenty-six taxa appeared in $$5/9 nested panels; core CRC-associated species including Parvimonas micra, Fusobacterium nucleatum, Peptostreptococcus stomatis and Gemella morbillorum were selected in all folds. US-CRC-2 remained weak (AUC $ 0.611$); excluding it raised mean LOCO AUC to 0.826. Conclusions. On public CRC metagenomes alone, nested species-panel modeling plus LOCO MRS yields a transparent, confounder-aware risk-scoring report with quantified transfer heterogeneity. abstract: Automated multi-class lesion detection in orthopantomogram (OPG) radiographs is challenged by small low-contrast findings, long-tailed class imbalance, and dense multi-tooth layouts. dataset: 口腔 OPG 多类病灶项目集
abstract: Automated multi-class lesion detection in orthopantomogram (OPG) radiographs is challenged by small low-contrast findings, long-tailed class imbalance, and dense multi-tooth layouts. Existing compact YOLO detectors provide practical throughput but leave a stage mismatch between deepest panoramic pooling and high-resolution P3 decoding. This paper proposes (Dual-Module Detector with BiFPNRefine and AdaptiveCBAM), a YOLOv8n detector that inserts BiFPNRefine for weighted multi-branch context refine at the backbone terminus and AdaptiveCBAM for sequential channel--spatial attention on P3. On the locked Dental OPG XRAY six-class split under a 640~px protocol, the YOLOv8n gate reaches 65.70\% mAP@0.5, while attains 78.67\% mAP@0.5 (+12.97~pp; singles 69.96\%/ 73.35\%; +18.82~pp over the strongest retained external comparator) under the class-imbalance-aware recipe. Controlled ablation, sibling-recipe analysis, and qualitative diagnostics support the dual-module design for OPG screening. dental radiography, orthopantomogram, object detection, YOLO, attention mechanism, ablation study

direction: 产后多检验轨迹恢复识别
dataset: 产后多检验时序 / 留出实验室验证
abstract: Postpartum physiological recovery is a multi-system process in which laboratory markers gradually return toward baseline after delivery. Distinguishing uncomplicated recovery from trajectories altered by major obstetric complications is clinically relevant, yet publicly reusable resources are often released as population-level weekly summaries rather than individual electronic medical records. This study analyzes the PregnancyMillions/Clalit aggregates derived from more than 300,000 pregnancies and focuses on postpartum-centered multi-lab dynamics. Uncomplicated and complication-conditioned cohorts are aligned at a common four-week resolution across 110 shared assays; single-assay curves and multi-assay panels are constructed under a lab-held-out protocol that prevents leakage from previously seen laboratory markers. We propose \ (Contrastive Lab-dynamics Attention Encoder), a temporal convolutional encoder with self-attention and supervised contrastive regularization, and compare it with feature-based ensembles and a broader suite of sequence models, including bidirectional recurrent networks with attention, temporal Transformers, PatchTST-style patch encoders, TCN/ResNet/InceptionTime variants, and TS-Mixer-style mixers. The experimental package further includes channel/window/panel ablations, temporal occlusion and noise robustness, attention and permutation explainability, decision-curve analysis, case-level error audit, system-held-out transfer, and multi-seed stability checks. Under a locked lab-held-out split, stronger sequence models can push binary AUROC to 0.919 (BiGRU) and 0.918 (BiLSTM-Attn), above Feature+RF (0.865); three-seed re-evaluation shows that BiGRU remains close to the tree baseline on average ($0.8620.027$), whereas Transformer peaks are seed-sensitive. Signal concentrates in postpartum/peripartum dynamics and dispersion features; panels substantially outperform singles; and cross-system hold-out remains difficult. The results show that population-level multi-lab trajectories retain informative signatures of postpartum recovery, while requiring leakage-aware evaluation, multi-seed reporting, and cautious interpretation when individual-level records are unavailable. postpartum recovery, laboratory dynamics, pregnancy complications, time-series recognition, lab-held-out evaluation, contrastive learning

abstract: Aging is a dominant risk factor for atrial fibrillation (AF), but single-cohort genome-wide transcriptomic screens often return unstable gene lists. Here we present MARAS-AF (Multi-database Aging-Related Atrial Signature for AF), a Type-A public-data workflow that restricts primary testing to an aging-related gene panel, requires concordant AF-versus-sinus-rhythm effects in two left-atrial discovery cohorts (GSE79768 and GSE41177), selects hubs only within discovery data, and uses external directional consistency as the primary replication endpoint across GSE115574, GSE14975, GSE2240, and exploratory GSE31821. The pipeline yielded 11 core aging-related differentially expressed genes (ARDEGs) and 10 hubs. MARAS-AF therefore nominates reproducible aging-linked AF candidates from public transcriptomes without claiming paired multi-omics or clinical diagnostic performance.

title: Left--Right Atrial Heterogeneity of Aging-Related Transcriptomic Signatures in Atrial Fibrillation

abstract: Aging-constrained multi-cohort screens of atrial fibrillation (AF) typically prioritize left atrium to reduce anatomical confounding, yet it remains unclear whether the recovered aging-AF signature is left-preferential or shared across atria. Here we present LATRAS-AF (Laterality of aging Transcriptomic Signature in AF), a Type-A public-data companion analysis that freezes the ten MARAS-AF hubs and tests side-stratified AF-versus-sinus-rhythm effects within a 227-gene aging panel in GSE115574 and GSE79768, with paired left/right atrial appendage RNA-seq from GSE128188 as an exploratory laterality layer. Paired GSE128188 supported direction for 7/10 hubs per side without hub-level paired LA$-$RA shifts at nominal $P<0.05$. These results support partial left enrichment of aging-panel differential density with largely shared hub polarity, without claiming a diagnostic device or matched multi-omics causality.

title: Cell-Type Localization of Aging-Related Atrial Fibrillation Hubs in Human Left-Atrial Appendage Single-Nucleus RNA-seq

abstract: Bulk multi-cohort transcriptomic screens can nominate aging-related atrial fibrillation (AF) hub genes, but they do not resolve which left-atrial cell types express those hubs. Following the bulk-to-single-nucleus assignment logic of recent LAA multiome studies, we present CELLOC-AF (Cell-type Localization of bulk AF hubs via LAA snRNA): a secondary analysis that freezes eleven aging hubs from the companion MARAS-AF multi-database workflow and assigns each gene to author-annotated cell types in the public scAF multiome series GSE238242 (11,986 nuclei; seven donors; left-atrial appendage). Using percent cells expressing as the primary localization metric, seven hubs mapped to cardiomyocytes (DNM1L, MAPK1, MAPK14, MAX, MDM4, PPARA, VEGFA), three to lymphoid cells (ATM, CASP8, CCR2), and TLR4 to endocardial cells. Marker sanity checks recovered expected lineage genes, and an exploratory AF-minus-sinus-rhythm expression delta is reported only descriptively because donor $n$ is small. CELLOC-AF therefore supplies cell-type context for aging AF hubs without claiming a new AF atlas, without re-selecting hubs from single-nucleus data, and without clinical diagnostic performance.

title: Development and Multicenter External Validation of an Artificial Intelligence Model for Opportunistic Osteoporosis Screening from Lumbar Radiographs

abstract: Opportunistic osteoporosis assessment from lumbar radiographs could extend screening beyond dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) capacity, yet radiograph signals are sparse, multi-scale, and strongly confounded by age, sex and body habitus. We developed , a ResNet18-based model that couples deformable multi-scale aggregation (DMSA) with clinical-guided affine fusion (CGAF) to predict World Health Organization three-class bone status and continuous T-scores on the public LUMOS cohort ($n=803$ patients). Under a patient-level held-out test and a strict joint ablation protocol, \ reached macro-AUC 0.836 versus 0.757 for the shared baseline, exceeding both single-module variants. Hospital data are reserved for locked multicenter external validation and are not used here. These results support clinically conditioned radiograph models as a reproducible development baseline for opportunistic DXA-anchored screening.
